FINAL_01_master_forest.caption: The 17 candidates of the cross-lane selection as their lanes deliver them (leave-one-person-out, 95 % person-bootstrap CIs), coloured by lane; open markers: chosen on the outer folds in their lane (exploratory, 7 of 17); diamonds: log loss after the calibration remedy chosen inside each fold (shown where it moves by more than 0.001); dashed: the reference floor. Lowest log loss as delivered: m3 1D CNN, body frame (0.291).
FINAL_01_master_forest.decision: Which candidates are worth a nested selection and a robustness check; the forest is exploratory, the nested estimate (FINAL_03) is the honest number.

FINAL_02_overview.caption: Every experiment of the model lanes' registries, the reference and this lane's own models (361 with a log loss below 1.2; this lane's stress tests are left out), accuracy against log loss; open markers: compared on the outer folds before being kept (n_configs_tried > 1, exploratory; 127); squares: lane m4, whose unit is a cue-free recording and whose abstentions score one half. Points near 50 % and a log loss of 0.69 are ablations that cannot see the hand by design (for example magnitude-only inputs).
FINAL_02_overview.decision: Context for the selection: the finalists sit on the accuracy / log-loss frontier of their lanes.

FINAL_03_nested_selection.caption: Nested cross-lane selection among 17 candidates: (left) how often each was chosen by the lowest inner log loss on the training persons, over 20 outer folds; (right) the selection-aware estimate against the best candidate picked on the outer folds (m3 1D CNN, body frame; 95 % person-bootstrap CIs). Optimism of the naive pick: accuracy +0.8 points [-0.2, +2.3], log loss -0.015.
FINAL_03_nested_selection.decision: The honest headline of the selection procedure is the nested number, not the best of the forest.

FINAL_04_paired.caption: Every candidate against the lowest-log-loss candidate (m3 1D CNN, body frame) on the same trials, each in its production form (its own pipeline plus the calibration remedy chosen inside every fold): mean per-person differences with paired person-bootstrap 95 % CIs; filled red: Holm-adjusted sign-flip p below 0.05 within the family (11 of 16 differ in accuracy or log loss).
FINAL_04_paired.decision: Which candidates the data cannot separate from the best: the leaders among which simplicity, robustness and portability decide.

FINAL_05_input_vs_class.caption: Input against model class (task 2b): paired accuracy differences (mean per person, 95 % person-bootstrap CI; filled red: Holm p below 0.05 over these comparisons) between models given the same channels.
FINAL_05_input_vs_class.decision: Whether the deep model's advantage needs the network or only the body-frame input.

FINAL_06_robustness.caption: Robustness of every candidate to test conditions the PI may choose (rows sorted by recorded accuracy; bold: the final model). Left: accuracy on the rotated-grip trials when trained on every grip (dot) or on upright grips only (square; 5 of 17 candidates drop with a Holm-adjusted p below 0.05). Middle: accuracy as recorded (dot) and on the same trials synthesised as held with the screen away, without (down triangle; 11 of 11 candidates whose inputs change drop significantly) and with the rest-pose screen check (up triangle; 11 of 11 back within 5 points of the recorded accuracy). Gravity-frame-only inputs are unchanged by the flip (dot only). Right: accuracy change when trained on the persons of the other platform only and when trained without the suspect wrong-hand blocks.
FINAL_06_robustness.decision: A model that is not robust to plausible test conditions is not the final model: device-frame models fail an unseen grip, and every model that reads the screen-relative frame needs the rest-pose check.

FINAL_07_natural_transfer.caption: Person-matched natural-use test: correct free-choice trials (dots; all reported hands are the right hand, so this is right-hand recall) against the count expected from the same persons' right-hand accuracy on the instructed trials (tick, 95 % Poisson-binomial range in grey); red: a shortfall after Holm over the candidates.
FINAL_07_natural_transfer.decision: A model whose evidence does not transfer to natural use relies on protocol-specific motion.

FINAL_08_calibration.caption: Reliability of the final model (m3 1D CNN, body frame), equal-mass bins with person-bootstrap 95 % bands, overall and per platform; shipped remedy: none. ECE 0.026 (perfect-calibration 95 % band up to 0.042), slope 0.97 [0.69, 1.50].
FINAL_08_calibration.decision: Whether the percentage shown to the user is honest, overall and on each platform.

FINAL_09_remedies.caption: Calibration remedies of the final model fitted on the training persons' inner cross-fitted predictions: paired per-person log-loss difference against no remedy (95 % CI; red: Holm p below 0.05 over the remedies). Shipped: none.
FINAL_09_remedies.decision: Ship a remedy only if it measurably lowers the log loss; prefer none or one parameter.

FINAL_10_attempts.caption: Several attempts of one person and hand (19 persons with at least 5 trials of each hand; random k-subsets within person and hand, the same persons for every k): over-confidence of four aggregates (left; mean confidence minus accuracy per person and hand, person-bootstrap 95 % bands; above 0: over-confident) and their log loss (right). The aggregates give nearly the same answers (accuracy at k = 3 between 96.3 and 96.3 %) and differ in the percentage shown. tau_k is fitted in every outer fold on the training persons' inner cross-fitted logits (median tau_3 1.54).
FINAL_10_attempts.decision: Which aggregate the page displays: a calibrated one; the mean P(right) is not shown.

FINAL_11_persons.caption: Final model by person (left; sorted; colour: platform; L: the 2 left-handed persons) and by grip x speed cell (right; the instructed conditions only stratify the predictions; person-bootstrap 95 % CI for cells with at least 5 persons; open markers: fewer persons, no CI, their persons' values are in the breakdown table).
FINAL_11_persons.decision: Which persons and conditions the final model fails on.

FINAL_12_learning_curve.caption: Learning curves: training persons drawn at random inside every outer fold (dots: repetitions; line: their mean; dashed: inverse power law with a 95 % bootstrap band). The inverse power law fitted to m3 1D CNN, body frame extrapolates to 89.6 % at 40 persons [88.8, 90.8] (bootstrap over repetitions; an extrapolation).
FINAL_12_learning_curve.decision: Whether recording more participants looks worthwhile.

FINAL_13_segmentation.caption: Final model trained on the oracle bounds and tested on windows cut with segmentation errors or a causal filter (lane p1's variant arrays, the same canonical code path): paired accuracy change with 95 % CIs (red: Holm p below 0.05).
FINAL_13_segmentation.decision: What the production detector must achieve: the bound accuracy the model tolerates.

FINAL_14_prior.caption: A deployment prior pi of the right hand adds log(pi / (1 - pi)) to every logit: right-hand recall rises, left-hand recall falls and the balanced accuracy drops (primary trials). The shipped default is pi = 0.5 (the PI chooses the hand).
FINAL_14_prior.decision: Keep the prior at 0.5 for the PI's evaluation.

FINAL_15_families.caption: One or two models of each family, each tested on participants it had never seen (leave-one-subject-out, LOSO): accuracy (left) and area under the ROC curve (right) with person-bootstrap 95 % CIs. The 1D CNN, the final model (blue), scores highest on both; the intervals of the best models overlap.
FINAL_15_families.decision: Shows which model family wins; the selection-aware estimate of the whole choice is the nested number (final/nested_accuracy), not the winner's own LOSO accuracy shown here.

FINAL_16_calibration.caption: Calibration before and after, for a model that needed it (top) and for the final model (bottom). (a) Raw scores against the observed share of right-hand trials, in ten equal-size groups of trials with similar scores (95 % person-bootstrap CI); the dashed diagonal is perfect calibration. (b) The fitted calibration function (Platt scaling, a logistic function of the score), fitted on the training participants of each LOSO fold. (c) The calibrated probabilities against the observed share.
FINAL_16_calibration.decision: What calibration does, shown where it mattered and on the final model, whose raw scores were already close to calibrated.

FINAL_17_attempts.caption: Combining k attempts of the same participant and hand (19 participants with at least 5 attempts of each hand; random draws of k attempts, each participant left out in turn): accuracy (left) and log loss (right, with 95 % person-bootstrap bands). The two ways of combining give nearly the same answers, but the average of the probabilities does not grow more confident as attempts accumulate, so its log loss stops improving.
FINAL_17_attempts.decision: The page shows the scaled sum of evidence; the mean P(right) is not shown.

FINAL_18_persons.caption: Accuracy of the final model on each participant when that participant was left out (LOSO), sorted; dark bars: Android, hatched: iPhone; L: the 2 left-handed participants; dashed: 80 %, which 3 participants fall below.
FINAL_18_persons.decision: Who the final model fails on.

FINAL_19_learning_curve.caption: Learning curve of the 1D CNN: inside every LOSO fold the model was retrained on 5 random draws of training participants of each size (grey dots; black: their mean; the point at 19 uses every training participant). Dashed: the fitted inverse power law with a 95 % band from resampling the draws; it extrapolates to 89.6 % at 40 participants.
FINAL_19_learning_curve.decision: Whether recording more participants of the same kind looks worthwhile.
